jobs.title: Housing Case Manager - Vista Nueva
jobs.description:
*We’re looking for dedicated team members to join Orange County’s largest nonprofit developer of high-quality affordable housing and services. Join us in our mission to transform lives and strengthen communities for thousands of families, seniors, veterans, transitional age youth, and individuals coming from homelessness in California.*

In this role, you will be working closely with individuals who are currently experiencing or transitioning from homelessness. This population often faces significant challenges, including difficulties adhering to societal norms related to hygiene, personal space, and polite conversation. We are looking for team members who can set boundaries with clients, while also being committed to fostering a supportive environment that promotes dignity, trust, and understanding.

Location: Sacramento, CA  
Status: Full Time, Hourly  
Wage: $23/hour + Benefits

**Primary Objective of Position:**

The Housing Case Manager will oversee programs fostering life skills, coping mechanisms, goal setting, and housing stability to program participants. Also provide linkage and referral services to residents to increase housing stability.

  

**Major Areas of Accountability:**

* Provide supportive services to address issues and barriers that negatively impact progress toward goals.
* Maintain responsibility for tenant rosters that show entry-exits for relevant Jamboree property.
* Monitor for warning signs of de-compensation and crisis, and responding accordingly.
* Record keeping, documenting and reporting as needed.
* Document resident participation in services and track progress of resident goals.
* Complete monthly newsletters describing the available social and supportive services offered on-site and off-site, including a calendar reflecting the time and location of such services.
* Maintain information regarding the off-site services and programs and provide referrals to such programs when appropriate.
* Provide advocacy, onsite case management services and linkage to residents as needed.
* Complete intake assessment and orientation with new residents.
* Maintain effective relations and coordinate services between community supports, service providers and property management.
* Provide a positive atmosphere for the residents and promote community engagement.
* Provide daily Adult Education groups/workshops onsite to residents.
* Plan and coordinate Health and Wellness events and community building activities yearly.
* Input data into the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) accurately and on a timely basis.
* Provide onsite life skills training and reinforcement to residents.
* Other duties as assigned.

  

**Level of Education, Experience and Skill Set:**

* Over 18 years of age.
* Experience working with individuals experiencing chronic homelessness and mental health challenges.
* Familiarity with the Housing First, Harm Reduction and/or Recovery Oriented service models.
* Ability to maintain relationships with other consumers/members while maintaining appropriate boundaries as a staff.
* Ability to interact in a culturally diverse community.
* AA degree preferred; or equivalent experience serving homeless individuals.
* Ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team setting and also independently.
* Knowledge of independent living skills such as cooking, budgeting, housekeeping, being a good neighbor, etc.
* Valid California driver’s license and availability of an insured vehicle.
* Job includes some evening and weekend hours and travel throughout California.

  

**Physical Demands:**

The Housing Case Manager is required to talk and hear. The employee is often required to sit and use their hands and fingers to handle or feel. The employee is required to stand, walk, reach with arms and hands, climb, balance, twist, lean, move from one location to another and to stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. Vision abilities required by this job include close and far vision. Ability to operate a computer keyboard, and lift files and reports. Exposure to glare from a computer.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Must be able to lift 25 lbs and travel by automobile 10%.

  

**Work Environment:**

Working with the homeless population whether on the streets, in shelters or other places of habitation or services. Exposure to bed bugs or other infestations, unpleasant smells or odors, unclean individuals or homes due to homelessness or mental health symptoms or poverty. Some work will be in a recreational room or common area. The noise level is usually moderate but will vary depending on the activity participating in.

Habitat Health empowers older adults to experience more good days in their homes and communities. Through the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), we provide comprehensive medical care along with support for daily needs such as meals, transportation, and in‑home assistance. We deliver coordinated clinical and social care in our centers and directly in participants' homes, creating a fully integrated experience that brings peace of mind and a true sense of belonging. As we expand our scalable, affordable PACE model to meet the growing and complex needs of aging populations, our mission‑driven care teams continue to help participants live well on their own terms.

Habitat Health is supported by leading healthcare organizations and investors including New Enterprise Associates, Kaiser Permanente, and Town Hall Ventures. We are entering a period of significant growth and are looking for exceptional teammates to help us scale a better model of care for older adults. To learn more, visit www.habitathealth.com.

**Estimated Start Date:** 11/2026

**Schedule:** Monday - Friday

**Location:** Sacramento Center

**Role Scope**:

The RN Care Manager delivers personalized, longitudinal nursing care to a panel of PACE participants, conducting face-to-face assessments across physical, psychosocial, and behavioral domains in both center and home settings, and partnering with medical providers to implement care plans. This role manages care coordination end-to-end, collaborating and coordinating with the entire care team as needed. As a collaborative participant and leader in Interdisciplinary Team (IDT) meetings, this role contributes clinical insights that inform whole-person care planning and educates participants, caregivers, and team members on carrying out personalized care plans — all while contributing to a center culture grounded in Habitat's values and participant belonging

* Contribute to a center experience that Participants want to spend time in, a team culture that cares and creates joy, and an environment where all participants and team members belong.
* Continue to raise the bar. Constructively seek and share feedback and help us implement changes in order to improve clinical outcomes and experience for participants.
* Exhibit and honor Habitat's Values.
* Participate n Interdisciplinary Team (IDT) meetings by contributing insights from assessments, care plan recommendations, and care coordination in a collaborative spirit.
* Conduct face-to-face nursing assessments that are inclusive of physical, psychosocial, and behavioral statuses in various settings, primarily in the Habitat center but also in–home as needed.
* In partnership with a medical provider, deliver personalized care for a panel of participants based on care plans.
* Deliver and document nursing interventions as agreed upon in participant's care plans, promptly and accurately responding to physician orders, and correctly administering medications and therapeutic interventions.
* Provide case management longitudinally and during transitions of care. Proactively coordinate complex patient discharges, transfers, and immediate post-discharge needs with hospital and long-term care facility case managers.
* Coordinate all aspects of care delivery including medication. management, medical equipment and supplies, and specialist and diagnostic referrals
* Triage in the outpatient setting, which includes independently initiating therapies within scope of practice and collaboratively working with a medical provider to escalate care as needed.
* Educate participants, caregivers including family members, and team members on how to personalize and carry out care plans.
* Aid with all wound care (including complex wounds), IV (hydration, therapies), and any additional procedures within RN scope of practice identified to meet evolving participant needs.

* Strong clinical acumen in chronic disease management and complex geriatric care.
* Demonstrates experience in management of clinical interventions: wound care, IVs, phlebotomy, colostomy/ileostomy care, etc.
* Proof of current CPR/BLS certification required or requirement to obtain within 30 days of employment.

**About AEG:**

At AEG, we're building something bigger than great eye care, we're creating careers, developing leaders, and making a meaningful difference in the communities we serve.

You'll join a team that:

* Invests in leadership development and internal growth.
* Believes people and performance go hand in hand.
* Values collaboration, authenticity, and continuous learning.
* Celebrates wins, supports challenges, and grows together.

**About the role**

The ability to anticipate needs, communicate clearly, and proactively manage the daily schedule helps ensure an efficient, high-quality experience for every patient.

* Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively across teams.

* Must be able to maintain patient and practice confidentiality.

* 401(k) with Match
* Medical/Dental/Vision/Life/STD/LTD

**Physical Demands**

* Ability to utilize office equipment

* Ability to lift up to 10 lbs

Do you want to be part of an innovative organization sustaining vulnerable, isolated seniors to EAT: Eat, Age, Thrive in Yolo County and regionally? Is the “why” you do your job a priority in your career? Then you may be the hero we’re seeking to provide nourishing meals and wellness checks to aging adults countywide and beyond lacking the access and/or the ability to dependably prepare their own healthy meals.  
  
MOW YOLO APPROACH  
Meals on Wheels Yolo County (“MOW Yolo”) is adding a Community Health Worker to our already inspired team. We are looking for a CHW who will:  

* Lead efforts with MOW Yolo seniors to identify their needs and connect them with appropriate resources and services.
* Prioritize nutritious food security and socialization so that seniors in the region may EAT: Eat, Age, Thrive.
* Positively represent MOW Yolo internally and externally

  
POSITION SUMMARY:  
The Community Health Worker (CHW) reports to the Programs Director and provides compassionate, person-centered support to seniors, ages 60 and older. The work of the CHW furthers MOW Yolo’s mission to nourish and engage vulnerable older adults and others with mobility challenges throughout Yolo County and beyond.  
  
USUAL WORK SCHEDULE:  
The CHW is a full-time (40 hours per week), non-exempt position, working Monday through Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm with some flexibility available based upon organizational needs. Primary work location is in the field at MOW Yolo Participant homes, congregate meal locations, and other sites throughout Yolo County, including the MOW Yolo Administrative office in Woodland and the MOW Yolo meal production facility in Winters.  
  
ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:  
1. Participant Intake & Assessment: Conduct person-centered assessments to identify participants’ needs, strengths, barriers, and goals.  
2. Participant Support & Follow-Up: Manage an assigned caseload of seniors, conduct regular check-ins and reassessments, and coordinate ongoing services to support health, independence, and safe aging in place.  
3. Resource Coordination & Referrals: Connect participants with appropriate community resources and supportive services, assist with referrals as needed, and maintain an up-to-date directory of senior-focused resources.  
4. Relationship Building & Community Engagement: Develop positive relationships with seniors, caregivers, volunteers, colleagues, and community partners while participating in outreach and strengthening awareness of MOW Yolo programs and services.  
5. Documentation, Communication & Professional Responsibilities: Maintain accurate case records and required documentation, communicate participant needs and emerging issues with supervisors and colleagues, attend staff meetings, and support evolving program needs.  
6. Supervise Community Navigator(s) in shared work responsibilities.  
  
QUALIFICATIONS:  
1. Education & Experience: High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s Degree in a related field preferred. Experience working with seniors and knowledge of aging-related needs preferred; outreach experience desirable.  
2. Physical Requirements: Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs., stand for extended periods, bend below the waist, and reach overhead.  
3. Independent & Adaptive Work: Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and respond flexibly, creatively, and patiently to varied and unexpected situations.  
4. Communication & Technology Skills: Ability to read, write, perform basic math, and accurately maintain records and reports. Proficiency with or willingness to learn electronic systems; Microsoft Office experience required, with Google Workspace familiarity preferred.  
5. Driving & Professional Standards: Valid California Class C driver’s license with a satisfactory driving record, maintained in good standing. Demonstrates professional hygiene, appearance, conduct, and demeanor.  
  
POSITION LICENSES/CERTIFICATIONS:  
1. Current California Driver’s License.  
2. Proof of current automobile insurance.  
3. Mandated Reporter Training, Mental Health First Aid Cert, BLS, Motivational Interviewing, (MOW Yolo pays for this training if needed).  
  
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS  
$26-$30 per hour (DOE), payable per the regular payroll schedule and subject to applicable withholding and payroll taxes and other deductions required by law. Full-time employees receive paid medical, dental, vision, vacation and sick time accrual, 11 paid holidays annually, and the option to participate in a 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan.  
  
\*\*This position is funded through a grant and is contingent upon the availability and continuation of grant funding.\*\*  
  
APPLICATION PROCEDURE AND TIMELINE  
Please submit your resume to HR@mowyolo.org. Applicant screening will be ongoing as the goal is to  
welcome a new team member as soon as possible.  
  
ABOUT MEALS ON WHEELS YOLO COUNTY  
Meals on Wheels Yolo County has a 50-year history as the only provider of fully-prepared meals for food insecure, isolated seniors in Yolo County, now nourishing 1,000 aging adults in both the cities and rural communities, as well as hundreds more regionally as part of MOW Yolo’s growing social enterprise operations. Core programs include:  

* Home-Delivered Meals (primarily volunteer delivered)
* Café Yolo Social Dining (congregate meals)
* Weekend Food Project (shelf-stable meals)
* MOW PAWS - Pets and Well Seniors (pet foods for isolated seniors’ furry companions)

MOW Yolo performs its mission according to a three-year strategic plan and sparks and engages in dozens of collaborations and partnerships throughout the region to sustain and elevate the opportunity for seniors to EAT: Eat, Age, Thrive and age in place healthily and safely, with independence and dignity.

At Marketplace Physical Therapy, our patients are at the center of what we do. Our Patient Care Coordinators play an important role in creating a welcoming, organized, and positive experience for every patient who walks through our doors.

We value **teamwork, professionalism, accountability, and people who take pride in their work.** If you enjoy helping people, staying busy, solving problems, and being part of a team, we'd love to have you join us.

### **About the Role**

We are looking for a **friendly, organized, and dependable Patient Care Coordinator** to join our team. This is a fast-paced, people-focused role for someone who enjoys helping others, staying busy, and keeping things running smoothly.

As a Patient Care Coordinator, you will be one of the main points of contact for our patients. You will welcome patients when they arrive, help manage their appointments, answer questions, communicate by phone, and help keep the front desk running efficiently.

The right person for this role is someone who can **multitask without losing attention to detail, communicate professionally and warmly, take initiative, and stay calm when things get busy.** Most importantly, you should genuinely enjoy helping people and making their experience a positive one.

### **What You'll Do**

* Welcome and greet patients in a professional, friendly, and enthusiastic manner.

* Check patients in and accurately document no-shows according to clinic guidelines.
* Schedule and manage patient appointments while following established scheduling guidelines.
* Help keep provider schedules full by utilizing available appointment times appropriately.
* Confirm upcoming evaluations and appointments.

This population often faces significant challenges, including difficulties adhering to societal norms related to hygiene, personal space, and polite conversation. Location: Sacramento, CA  
Status: Full Time, Hourly  
Wage: $23/hour + Benefits

The Housing Case Manager will oversee programs fostering life skills, coping mechanisms, goal setting, and housing stability to program participants. Also provide linkage and referral services to residents to increase housing stability.

* Provide supportive services to address issues and barriers that negatively impact progress toward goals.
* Maintain responsibility for tenant rosters that show entry-exits for relevant Jamboree property.
* Monitor for warning signs of de-compensation and crisis, and responding accordingly.
* Record keeping, documenting and reporting as needed.
* Document resident participation in services and track progress of resident goals.
* Complete monthly newsletters describing the available social and supportive services offered on-site and off-site, including a calendar reflecting the time and location of such services.

* Complete intake assessment and orientation with new residents.
* Maintain effective relations and coordinate services between community supports, service providers and property management.
* Provide a positive atmosphere for the residents and promote community engagement.
* Provide daily Adult Education groups/workshops onsite to residents.
* Plan and coordinate Health and Wellness events and community building activities yearly.

* Provide onsite life skills training and reinforcement to residents.

At SCAN, we believe scale should strengthen—not dilute—our mission. We are building the future of care for older adults, grounded in purpose, accountability, and respect for the people and communities we serve.

* Utilize department desktop procedures, workflows, job aids and training material.
* Performs work under direct supervision. Handles basic issues and problems and refers more complex issues to higher-level staff.
* Possesses beginning-to-working knowledge of subject matter.

* Actively support the achievement of SCAN’s Vision and Goals.
* Other duties as assigned.

* 0-3 years working in healthcare/customer service.
* Use motivational interviewing techniques to understand and accurately address member concerns.
* Ability to work in an environment where continuous coaching and feedback is the standard practice.
* Basic interpersonal skills, including excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Basic organizational skills.
* Basic critical thinking skills.
* Ability to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
* Ability to appropriately maintain confidentiality.
* General understanding of CMS and DHCS regulations.
* General knowledge of medical terminology and abbreviations.
* General knowledge of local community resources for seniors.
* Spanish strongly preferred Conversational (Oral), Reading, Writing.
* Microsoft Office skills (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Team) are required.

* Base wage range: $21.78 to $26.00 per hour.
* Work Mode: Mostly Remote
* An annual employee bonus program

* Generous paid-time-off (PTO)

* Robust employee recognition program

* An opportunity to become part of a team that makes a difference to our members and our community every day!

Description:

### **Why Marketplace Physical Therapy?**

At Marketplace Physical Therapy, our patients are at the center of what we do. Our Patient Care Coordinators play an important role in creating a welcoming, organized, and positive experience for every patient who walks through our doors.

We value **teamwork, professionalism, accountability, and people who take pride in their work.** If you enjoy helping people, staying busy, solving problems, and being part of a team, we'd love to have you join us.

### **About the Role**

We are looking for a **friendly, organized, and dependable Patient Care Coordinator** to join our team. This is a fast-paced, people-focused role for someone who enjoys helping others, staying busy, and keeping things running smoothly.

As a Patient Care Coordinator, you will be one of the main points of contact for our patients. You will welcome patients when they arrive, help manage their appointments, answer questions, communicate by phone, and help keep the front desk running efficiently.

The right person for this role is someone who can **multitask without losing attention to detail, communicate professionally and warmly, take initiative, and stay calm when things get busy.** Most importantly, you should genuinely enjoy helping people and making their experience a positive one.

### **What You'll Do**

* Welcome and greet patients in a professional, friendly, and enthusiastic manner.
* Provide excellent customer service in person and over the phone.
* Check patients in and accurately document no-shows according to clinic guidelines.
* Schedule and manage patient appointments while following established scheduling guidelines.
* Help keep provider schedules full by utilizing available appointment times appropriately.
* Confirm upcoming evaluations and appointments.
* Follow up with patients who miss appointments and help them get back on track with their care.
* Answer incoming calls and respond to patient questions and requests.
* Return and document voicemail messages within 24 hours.
* Document clear and accurate notes in patient charts.
* Collect patient payments, including copays, by credit card, debit card, cash, or check.
* Accurately enter payments into designated systems.
* Monitor the waiting room and make sure patients are acknowledged and assisted promptly.
* Maintain the lost patient log, payment log, waitlist, and online appointment requests.
* Keep the front desk and workstation clean, organized, and welcoming.
* Work closely with the clinic team to help ensure a smooth patient experience.
* Perform additional duties as needed.

Requirements:

### **What We're Looking For**

You don't need years of experience to be successful in this role. **We are looking for the right attitude, work ethic, and willingness to learn.**

The ideal candidate:

* Has a high school diploma or equivalent.
* Is comfortable using computers and learning new software.
* Has strong attention to detail and takes pride in doing things correctly.
* Is friendly, professional, and comfortable communicating with patients in person and over the phone.
* Can build rapport and make patients feel welcomed and cared for.
* Is dependable, organized, and able to manage multiple priorities at once.
* Can think through problems and troubleshoot with minimal assistance.
* Adapts well when schedules, priorities, or patient needs change.
* Takes initiative and looks for ways to help without always being asked.
* Is willing to jump in, support the team, and go the extra mile for our patients.
* Can remain professional, positive, and patient in a busy environment.

### **What Success Looks Like**

A successful Patient Care Coordinator is someone who **keeps the front desk moving, notices what needs to be done, communicates clearly, and makes patients feel taken care of.**

You may be answering a phone call while checking in a patient, adjusting a schedule, and helping another patient with a question. We need someone who can **prioritize, stay organized, and keep a positive attitude even when things get busy.**

This position is primarily sedentary and requires the ability to sit for extended periods, with occasional standing, walking, bending, crouching, kneeling, reaching, and lifting or carrying items weighing up to 10 pounds.

The position also requires frequent use of a computer and other office equipment, including repetitive movements of the hands, wrists, and fingers, as well as the ability to communicate clearly and receive verbal information in a typical office environment.
